one_liner: Pitt degree planner that pairs a 12-term timeline with a live requirement checker and a searchable, per-credit-priced database of 43,239 transfer equivalencies from 1,801 schools, plus a cost-optimizing 'Autocomplete my degree' that reroutes courses to cheaper schools.
problem: Students plan degrees in spreadsheets and only discover the cost when the bill arrives; transfer credit from cheaper schools could cut tuition but Pitt's equivalency data is unsearchable and unpriced.
target_user: University of Pittsburgh undergraduates (currently CS BS only), modelled as PA residents.
core_loop: User adds Pitt courses or transfer equivalencies (search by Pitt course, sorted cheapest-first, % online filter) into a 4-year Fall/Spring/Summer grid -> in-browser engine re-evaluates major + gen-ed requirements and cost (Pitt flat $12,322 at 12+ credits, $1,026/credit below; transfers billed at the home school's residency-aware per-credit rate) -> 'Autocomplete my degree' picks courses for every unmet requirement and sweeps 'transfer the cheapest k' to exploit the flat-rate cliff -> preview modal shows all-at-Pitt price struck through vs optimized total -> apply/undo. Optional PeopleSoft What-If PDF import seeds the plan.
mocked_or_hardcoded: Pitt tuition constants hardcoded; single major (CS BS) with a scaffold dropdown; most catalog credits default to 3; per-credit cost is derived (annual tuition/30) and fuzzy-name matched (1,696 of 1,801 schools priced); PDF import contains a documented DEMO HARDCODE that routes specific transfer courses to named schools; hidden Ctrl+D demo panel loads two canned sample plans (they still run through the real engine); no prerequisite checking; Express server and student-plan.json are legacy, production is fully static.
demo_risks: Low: no backend, no API keys, no LLM. The 12MB equivalency JSON loads lazily on first transfer search/autocomplete (a few seconds on venue wifi). PDF import only works on the PeopleSoft What-If format and carries demo-specific routing.
ui_experience: Polished pastel 'aged paper' theme with hand-drawn inline-SVG seasonal art per term card (drifting leaves, swaying flowers, sun over dunes), animated count-up cost hero with light sweep, SVG progress ring, requirement pills bar, shadcn modals for course/term picking, autocomplete preview with per-term picks and savings hero, undo toast. ~15 components, 2 tabs. Fully touchable in a demo.
integrity_flags: First commit (Sep 19 21:33, ~10.5h after start) already contained a complete MVP with a 'Redesign frontend' message, so earlier iterations were unversioned, though the timestamp is inside the event. Real Pitt equivalency data and IPEDS cost data (1,725 schools) shipped in-repo. No secrets committed. No starter-kit reuse detected. README names no tracks.
ai_scaffolding_flags: .gitignore excludes 'Claude outputs/' (Claude-assisted build); code comments are long LLM-style essays; no CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/handoff docs; docs are smaller than code.
novelty_notes: Degree planners are a common category; the twist is real: pricing every transfer equivalency with per-credit cost and online share, and an optimizer that understands Pitt's flat-rate cliff (moving one course out of a full term saves nothing, so it sweeps cutoffs instead of greedy per-course). No LLM anywhere.
need_notes: Specific, credible pain (tuition cost, opaque transfer credit) backed by real data volume, but evidence of demand is the founders' own student experience; only CS BS is modelled; per-credit prices are estimates.
wow_moment: Click 'Autocomplete my degree' on an empty planner: four years fill in, the all-at-Pitt price appears struck through next to a lower optimized total, and specific CCAC summer courses show $252/credit vs Pitt's $1,026.
score_rationale: Common category with a genuine new mechanism (S1 7). Real pain, real data, no demand evidence beyond authors (S2 7). Strong Seed Round and No Wrapper fit, credible .Tech stack; Compound only partial (S3 7). Static, real data path, error/loading states, undo, polished, but hardcoded tuition, demo hardcode in import, no tests (S4 12). Attractive animated UI, interactive, nothing physical (S5 9). One clear 'neat' savings reveal (wow 6).
judge_summary: A Pitt degree planner that prices 43k real transfer equivalencies and auto-fills a cheaper four-year plan, showing the all-Pitt price struck through next to the optimized total. Fully static, no LLM, polished seasonal UI. Single major only and tuition constants are hardcoded, but the savings reveal is memorable.

one_liner: Autonomous cancellation recovery for clinics: an ElevenLabs voice agent captures patients' scheduling intent, Nemotron extracts/ranks/decides, and when a slot is cancelled the system phones the best-fit patient via ElevenLabs+Twilio, cascades on decline or timeout, and falls back to policy-checked incentives.
problem: Last-minute cancellations leave paid appointment slots empty; waitlists store availability rather than intent, and staff have no time to phone around, so revenue evaporates.
target_user: Appointment-based small businesses (dental/medical clinic primary; tutoring and barber profiles seeded) and their patients.
stack: NVIDIA NIM via OpenAI SDK (nemotron-3-super-120b, fallback nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b)
ElevenLabs Conversational AI (browser agent + phone agent)
core_loop: Patient speaks to the ElevenLabs agent (browser widget or phone) -> save_scheduling_intent tool POSTs raw words -> Nemotron extracts hard constraints/soft preferences in a background task (plus a critique pass) -> owner cancels a booking on the calendar (or a patient cancels by voice) -> slot freed atomically -> deterministic eligibility filter (excluded days, providers, expiry) -> Nemotron ranks survivors -> Nemotron decide_outreach + generate_call_brief -> if the business profile has auto_call_enabled, ElevenLabs places a real outbound call with dynamic variables -> a 3s scheduler polls ElevenLabs for call end; booked-by-them = accepted, ended-without-booking = declined -> queue advances; on exhaustion Nemotron picks an incentive from the allowed list, backend validates it against max discount/revenue floor/excluded services, and re-offers -> calendar polls every 2s and shows stage badges.
mocked_or_hardcoded: DEMO_CALL_OVERRIDE_NUMBER routes every outbound call to one Twilio-verified number; 'Dr. Lee week' seed with scripted patient preference texts and an unauthenticated /api/dev/seed reset; seeded profiles set auto_call_enabled=True and 15-40s offer timeouts; frontend falls back to clearly labelled sample metrics/appointments/candidates when the API is unreachable; mock_store PATIENTS still back the legacy /api/recovery/plan playground route; the Gemini 'world-understanding' layer from the original plan is dead code (never imported); recent_declines fatigue signal hardcoded 0; voice_service.py is empty; README video path is wrong (docs/slotsaver.mp4 exists).
demo_risks: High external surface: NVIDIA NIM rate limits (ranking measured 10-40s, with model fallback), ElevenLabs, Twilio trial ('press any key' preamble, only verified numbers callable), Render free tier ~1 min cold start (mitigated by a 10-min GitHub Actions ping), Vercel/Render CORS env. Failures degrade gracefully (eligible-but-unranked, ranking_failed retry) rather than crash. Hindi extraction known broken. Fix commits landed until 10:48 on deadline day.
ui_experience: Clean indigo/white SaaS dashboard (Inter): sidebar, live metric cards, animated 'Scout' bunny mascot with states, week calendar grid where cancelling a booking opens a recovery panel that polls live ranking (scores + reasons), stage badges like 'Calling candidate 2 of 4' / 'Incentive offer', outreach queue, business-profile/incentive settings page, browser voice-agent page with live state indicator. ~10 components, 5 pages. Judges can cancel a slot and receive the phone call.
integrity_flags: All 111 commits inside the event window (Sep 19 13:31 to Sep 20 10:48). No secrets in git (.env.example only; render.yaml marks keys sync:false), though HANDOFF admits the ElevenLabs key leaked in chat transcripts and was not rotated; agent IDs and phone number are committed. Destructive seed and call-placing endpoints are unauthenticated (acknowledged). Paper's Gemini arm is n=23 with 42 quota errors, so its 95.7% is weak; earlier self-labelled N=5 RecoveryBench is explicitly disowned in docs. README names no tracks; sponsor use is implied.
ai_scaffolding_flags: Heavy: HANDOFF.md is addressed to 'the next Claude Code session'; TEAM_INSTRUCTIONS.md and FOLDER_STRUCTURE.md are file-ownership maps for three developers running Claude Code in parallel; commit messages and comments are LLM-style essays; HANDOFF states Claude authored benchmark scenarios, labels and prompts. Docs ~60KB md + 22KB tex versus ~10.4k source lines, so code still outweighs docs.
novelty_notes: Waitlist auto-fill tools exist commercially, but storing extracted scheduling intent (hard vs soft constraints, expiry) and closing the loop with autonomous outbound voice calls plus a policy-bounded incentive fallback is a distinctive combination. The side paper on output-token-ceiling confounds in NATURAL PLAN (Nemotron 84.6% at 4096 tokens, paired McNemar, n=65/model) is unusual rigor for a hackathon.
need_notes: Specific buyer (clinic owner), quantified pain ($120 per empty slot), three business profiles suggest generality; evidence is framing and seeded scenarios, no interviews or quotes.
wow_moment: Owner clicks cancel on a calendar booking; within ~30s the panel shows Nemotron's ranked patients with reasons, then a judge's phone actually rings with an ElevenLabs receptionist offering the slot; decline it and the panel visibly moves to candidate 2 with a discount spoken aloud.
score_rationale: Distinctive intent-memory plus autonomous voice cascade (S1 7). Specific buyer and dollar pain, no external validation (S2 7). Nemotron as non-chat decision engine with a real public benchmark, documented failures, stacked with voice-first ElevenLabs and revenue recovery (S3 8). Loop is real end to end with tests, scheduler, race guards and graceful degradation, but demo relies on trial-Twilio override and seeded data (S4 12). Clean dashboard plus a live phone call (S5 12). Phone ringing is a strong wow (8).
judge_summary: Cancel a clinic appointment on the dashboard and a real phone rings: Nemotron ranked the patients, ElevenLabs is offering the slot, and if they decline it moves to the next person with an approved discount. Real, well-guarded pipeline with a public Nemotron benchmark, but fragile on stage (NIM rate limits, trial Twilio, Render cold starts).
